entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Teti, also known as Othoes in Manetho's Aegyptiaca, ascended to the throne of Egypt around 2345 BCE, initiating the Sixth Dynasty, a pivotal period marking the final flowering of the Old Kingdom before its eventual fragmentation. His reign, believed to have lasted approximately 12 years until his death around 2333 BCE, represented a crucial moment of dynastic transition, consolidating royal authority after the somewhat turbulent late Fifth Dynasty and setting the stage for the powerful nomarchs who would increasingly challenge central control. He inherited a sophisticated administrative apparatus centered in Memphis, overseeing a vast realm stretching from the Nile Delta to the First Cataract at Aswan, a testament to the enduring stability and prosperity of the Old Kingdom's zenith.

During his tenure, Teti focused on maintaining the elaborate state bureaucracy and the extensive cultic practices essential for royal legitimacy. His most enduring physical legacy is his pyramid complex at Saqqara, located north of the step pyramid of Djoser. This complex, comprising a main pyramid, a mortuary temple, and a satellite pyramid, became the second pharaonic burial site to feature the Pyramid Texts inscribed on its interior walls, a collection of ancient Egyptian religious spells intended to guide the deceased king through the afterlife. These texts provide invaluable insights into Old Kingdom cosmology and royal funerary beliefs, demonstrating the king's divine role and his journey to eternal life among the stars.
